Theory of Computation is absolutely essential in any computer science program. I don't understand how it's not a core course. A decade or two ago, ToC would have been one of the few courses to be offered in any CS degree anywhere in the world. And nowadays it's becoming a second-class course in lieu of the more "industry-oriented" courses, which, btw, fail to be much useful in giving students the necessary skills to do well in the software industry. Sad to see CSE programs becoming substandard SWE programs.
Anywho, if you do choose to take CSE273, which you should, consider taking ARA2 sir's section. He's one of the more brilliant and true-to-the-field faculties I've come across in NSU. Also, if your goal is to secure a top grade but you're willing to be somewhat sincere about working for it, then his classes and homeworks will be more than enough to prepare you for the exams. Best of luck!
